title: The Protection of Information in Computer Systems — Basic Principles of Information Protection
publisher: Jerome H. Saltzer and Michael D. Schroeder; MIT author-hosted copy
claim: Protection should default to denial, mediate every access, minimize privilege, and keep enforcement mechanisms simple enough to analyze.
limit: These are established design principles, not evidence that SideFX satisfies them in every deployment.

title: Reference monitor — CSRC Glossary
date: Undated glossary; definition cites SP 800-53 Rev. 5 (2020)
claim: A reference validation mechanism should always mediate access, resist tampering, and be small enough for analysis and testing.
limit: SideFX's non-bypassability, tamper resistance, and verifiability require implementation evidence.

title: CHERI Frequently Asked Questions
publisher: University of Cambridge Computer Laboratory, CHERI project
claim: Capability systems restrict executing code to objects for which it holds authority, with enforcement possible at multiple system layers.
limit: A business capability is not automatically an unforgeable security capability or evidence of CHERI protection.

title: Advanced Topics — Proving Safety Properties; Hiding, Refinement, and Auxiliary Variables
claim: Refinement relates an implementation to a higher-level specification, while machine-checked proofs require work beyond informal correctness arguments.
limit: Tests, hashes, deterministic execution, and provenance records are not themselves formal proofs.

title: Getting Started with Dafny: A Guide
date: Undated maintained guide using Dafny 4 syntax
claim: Dafny verifies that code satisfies stated preconditions and postconditions, which express behavioral requirements beyond ordinary type constraints.
limit: Schema validation and correct implementation of an incomplete specification do not establish real-world safety.

title: Certification Strategies using Run-Time Safety Assurance for Part 23 Autopilot Systems
publisher: Loyd R. Hook et al.; NASA Technical Reports Server
claim: Runtime verification and independent safety mechanisms can support assurance of complex autopilot behavior and supplement certification.
limit: This is an engineering precedent, not evidence that SideFX has aviation certification or physical-control guarantees.

title: Guidance on the Implementation of an Objectives-Driven, Risk-Informed, and Case-Assured Framework for Safety and Mission Success
claim: Safety assurance connects explicit risk objectives to an evolving argument supported by evidence throughout a program's lifecycle.
limit: A demonstration alone does not establish a safety case across domains, hazards, and operating conditions.

title: PostgreSQL Documentation, 3.4 Transactions
claim: A database transaction commits a group of changes together or rolls them back while hiding incomplete intermediate states from other transactions.
limit: A database transaction does not automatically undo external API effects or provide exactly-once provider execution.

title: PROV-Overview — An Overview of the PROV Family of Documents
claim: Provenance records entities, activities, and responsible agents involved in producing artifacts so their derivation and trustworthiness can be assessed.
limit: Provenance alone does not prove factual truth, provide tamper evidence, or establish SideFX's PROV conformance.

title: Designing AI agents to resist prompt injection
publisher: OpenAI; Thomas Shadwell and Adrian Spânu
claim: Agent systems should constrain the consequences of manipulation even when it succeeds, including through deterministic limits outside the model.
limit: This corroborates the engineering problem and principle, not OpenAI endorsement or unique invention by SideFX.

title: How we contain Claude across products
claim: Environmental isolation, egress controls, credential separation, and granular tool permissions complement probabilistic model defenses.
limit: Provider isolation and infrastructure security remain necessary considerations; this source does not show that SideFX makes sandboxing obsolete.

title: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework (AI RMF 1.0)
claim: The voluntary AI RMF organizes continuous risk work under Govern, Map, Measure, and Manage, including documented evaluation and limitations.
limit: An architecture mapping is not NIST certification or complete framework compliance; a revision is in progress at access.

title: United Nations adopts ground-breaking Pact for the Future to transform global governance
publisher: United Nations Department of Global Communications
claim: The adopted Global Digital Compact includes commitments to AI governance, data governance, scientific assessment, and international dialogue.
limit: This establishes cooperation context, not UN endorsement or selection of SideFX; official indexed text was checked after direct fetch returned 403.

title: Independent International Scientific Panel on AI
claim: The UN established a scientific panel and Global Dialogue on AI Governance to connect independent scientific evidence with international deliberation.
limit: Collaboration is an invitation, not an existing relationship; official indexed content was verified while direct pages used access protection.

title: Defeating Prompt Injections by Design
publisher: Edoardo Debenedetti et al., Google, Google DeepMind and ETH Zurich
claim: CaMeL separates planning from untrusted data processing and enforces data-flow policies through an interpreter at tool calls.
limit: Its guarantees depend on a stated threat model, policies, trusted prompts and implementation assumptions. It is not a proof of SideFX or a universal AI-safety result.
